geometry_notes: E2 is one ~118 m bar (W2+W13 north, W4+W8 south, collinear pairs) with the finned south wing W5/W7 and a low north block W0/W1/W14 between the bar and E3.
W0 lies exactly on E3 W12 and W9/W10/W11 exactly on CPH W3/W2/W1: party walls, draw nothing there.

North block heights: lidar 5.1-5.4 m along W1 (1 storey) but 7.4-7.7 m along W14 (2 storeys); W0 falls 7.6 -> 5.2 m. The block is two-height: a 2-storey east part on the E3 courtyard and a 1-storey west part on the loading yard.
W2 side grade is ~1 m higher than W4 side (lidar 10.6 vs 11.5); use the 11.5 m roof and let W2 start higher, or use 10.6 for W2 as given.

South-west corner: lidar is ground (0.1 m) at W6 s 1-3, 2 m inside the footprint, and the arcade corner is open under the canopy (sv_W5_CEl5): the footprint's SW corner is ~2-3 m too generous or is an open undercut corner.
Roof penthouse (lidar ~13-13.5 m) missing from the footprint walls: see roof.

W0.summary: party wall: the line of E3 W12 (its s 35.6-60.9) runs exactly on this wall; E3's lab wall stands against E2's low north block here, so nothing of E2 shows
W0.notes: E3 W12.b = E2 W0.a = (1177.51, 244.75) and both lie on the same line; lidar inside falls 7.6 -> 5.2 m from a to b (E3 spec also notes its W12 drops to 5.5-6 m at s 42-50). Do not draw a facade; whichever building is drawn first should own this block. sv_W0_* panos look at E3/the E3 courtyard, not at this wall.

W2.summary: north face of the west wing on the E3 service yard: 3 storeys of buff brick with 13 full-height window strips (dark head, two glass tiers, dark spandrel) between brick piers, pale concrete floor bands; the east 8 m is blank brick with a grey louvre on the top floor over the loading dock
attached: loading dock platform s 0-6.5 (1.0 m, concrete with rusty steel edge), steel stair with black railing down at s ~6.5-8
small wall lamps over the ground-floor strips at s ~12 and ~17 (sv_W2_4Azf)
rain leader down the brick at s ~2
W2.notes: sv_W2_XrEJ (Aug 2015), sv_W2_4Azf/GA2D/-NQW (Jul 2019), sv_c0 (Sep 2014, west end). Ground here is ~1 m higher than on the south side, so the ground-floor strips start ~0.45 m above grade with no visible spandrel (lidar 10.2-10.7 m vs 11.5 on W4). Strip ~1.6 m wide, pitch ~3.75 m (W13 Earth count and sv_W4 measure agree). Top floor of the louvre bay is a grey metal louvre ~1.6 x 3 m; floors 1-2 of the east 8 m are blank brick with vertical control joints. Big pines 4-8 m out hide most of the middle.

W3.summary: west end wall on the PHY lane: blank buff brick with recessed vertical control joints and the pale concrete floor bands carried round; PHY's two-storey glazed bridge lands at s 9.7-12.5, a glazed door with a narrow window strip above just south of it

Control-joint piers are drawn as flush dark lines (brick_buff_sun stands in for the shadowed joint).

W4.summary: south face of the west wing on the Rod Coutts Hall plaza: 3 storeys of buff brick, 16 full-height window strips (dark navy head and spandrel panels, white-framed two-tier windows) between 2.15 m brick piers, pale concrete floor bands
attached: concrete retaining wall and short stair down (yellow nosings, steel handrail) along s ~3-10, 1-3 m out (sv_W4_gbQm; PHY spec mentions it)
small bronze wall lamp between strips at level 2 (sv_W4_eihW, s ~31)
W4.notes: sv_W4_eihW/si44/_H6I (Sep 2014, square-on, 6 m away): storey 235 px for 3.55 m; strip 1.6 m (window glass 1.5), pier ~2.1 m, pitch ~3.7 m; per storey from bottom: dark spandrel 0.9, white-framed window 2.0 (upper tier often curtained, lower tier two leaves), dark head 0.45, concrete band 0.2. Earth W4_whole and corner_3/5 show 3 storeys of strips the whole length (orange-buff in sunlight). Grass runs right up to the ground-floor spandrels. Lidar 11.4-11.6 m; the 13.5 m at s 6 is a tree.

W5.summary: the signature face: west side of the south wing on the RCH plaza. Ground floor is a white-columned glass arcade under a folded-plate concrete canopy whose shallow gables give a zig-zag fascia; above, two storeys of buff brick spandrels and window ribbons behind a dense row of tall pale precast fins (~4 per bay). Main entrance (ENGINEERING 2) in the second bay

fins.shape: precast blades standing ~0.5 m proud, flush with the coping at the top; each blade's lower end hangs ~0.6 m into the brick spandrel under the level-2 windows and is cut off square. arch.py fins() is the nearest helper (draw over the brick/window rows, not as a curtain wall).

folded_canopy.look: folded-plate concrete canopy: between each pair of white columns the soffit folds up to a ridge at mid-bay, so from the front it reads as a row of shallow gables (a zig-zag fascia) over the ground-floor glass; glazing follows the gable (pointed head)

attached: reflecting pool along the arcade (2014 SV), now paved with a row of planters (2023/2025 orthos): s ~8-20, 1-4 m out
small pool left of the entrance walk s ~0-3 (2014)
W5.notes: sv_W5_fEhx (entrance, Sep 2014), sv_W5_8yRm (square-on, 5 m), sv_W5_3efv/Y8qB/vFAm, sv_W5_CEl5 (south end), sv_c2-c4/c7-c9; Earth W5_whole/W7_whole. Column bays ~3.9 m (18 across 70 m in Earth); fin count by periodicity on Earth W5_whole and W7_whole is ~75 over the wall (pitch ~0.95 m, 4 per bay); the head-on 8yRm reads ~3 per bay, so pitch 0.95-1.3 m - use 0.975. Heights from fEhx/5OQp scaled to the 11.5 m lidar: ground to canopy top 3.9, brick 1.1, window 1.8, brick 1.9, window 1.8, brick parapet 1.0. Ground glass: 4 lites per bay, transom at ~2/3, dark bottom panels, set back under the canopy; columns white ~0.45 m. Entrance position: ortho 2025 shows the light entrance paving at s ~3-9 and fEhx shows it in the 2nd column bay; the 1st bay is partly tucked behind the W4 wing corner. The custom keys 'fins' and 'folded_canopy' carry the two features the cell grid cannot.
